http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30116v1.title: Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30116v1.abstract: Through a tangle of real-world interactions, from synthetic training pipelines to data shared on the open web, frontier LLMs absorb what their predecessors and competitors create. How well does each model play its role in this ecosystem, as a creator and as a solver? We introduce Environment Duels, a dynamic agentic benchmark that evaluates both capabilities on interactive environments. Each model writes environments, each with a privileged hint, aiming for tasks that capable solvers fail without the hint and pass with it. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29792v1.title: MAPS: Macro-Adaptive Parallel Reasoning for Regulating Search Momentum in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29792v1.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) improves the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) by retrieving external knowledge. Recently, some RAG methods interleave reasoning and retrieval, enabling LLMs to progressively generate sub-queries and retrieve external knowledge. However, these methods may suffer from redundant or ineffective sub-queries and insufficiently diverse query exploration. Moreover, due to the tightly interleaved nature of reasoning and retrieval, it remains unclear how the evolving reasoning process influences query intent. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29870v1.title: PAUSE: Search-Free Steering of Coding Agents Before Their First Source-Code Edit
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29870v1.abstract: Coding agents can invest substantial effort in repository exploration and testing yet still produce unsuccessful patches. Existing online steering methods review trajectories periodically or invoke an advisor when a monitor detects behavioral problems; frequent reviews are costly, and the absence of anomalous behavior does not mean that an agent is on the right track. We propose PAUSE, a framework for steering coding agents with a single planning intervention. Agents reach their first source-code edit at a median of 60% of trajectory progress, after exploration, bug reproduction, and testing.

http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30047v1.title: SWE-DIVE: Multi-Turn Coding Agent Evaluation with Dynamic User Simulation
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30047v1.abstract: Coding agents are typically evaluated using one-shot, well-formulated prompts. Benchmarks such as SWE-bench use existing GitHub issues as input for a coding agent and evaluate whether the agent successfully solves the task. However, in real-world use cases, prompts are often not as well-formulated or structured as existing GitHub issues. Additionally, a coding agent session is not limited to a single prompt; it typically involves a multi-turn interaction in which the user iteratively adds new tasks and requirements that the agent must fulfill. To benchmark these abilities, we developed SWE-DIV

http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29812v1.title: Real PMIDs, Wrong Papers: Harness Design for Biomedical Claim-Verification Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29812v1.abstract: Literature-searching language agents are becoming a standard component of scientific assistants for the life sciences, yet there is little controlled evidence on which parts of their harness matter. We run a controlled ablation on biomedical claim verification (SciFact) with the live PubMed API as the only tool. Holding the backbone and output format fixed, we compare four harnesses: closed-book answering, single-shot retrieval using the claim as the query, a ReAct-style agent that writes its own PubMed queries, and an oracle given the gold abstracts, each with two efficient frontier backbones

http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30051v1.title: From Reasoning to Action: Benchmarking Frontier AI Models on LIBERO-10 Robot Manipulation Tasks
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30051v1.abstract: Recent advances in frontier AI models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in visual understanding, reasoning, planning, and tool use, raising the possibility of using general-purpose AI models for robot manipulation without task-specific training. However, their manipulation capabilities have not been systematically evaluated on standardized robotics benchmarks. In this report, we present a unified closed-loop manipulation framework for evaluating frontier AI models on the LIBERO-10 benchmark. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30041v1.title: Robust Soft Skill Adaptation via Behavioral Localization in Tool-Using Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30041v1.abstract: Text skills can extend the capabilities of tool-using agents, but long skill descriptions increase computational costs. Soft prompts provide a compact alternative, yet learning from entire successful trajectories may also introduce unnecessary behavioral changes. We find that the useful effect of a text skill is highly concentrated in a small subset of trajectory positions. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30014v1.title: Agent Behavior Maps: Locating Agents by What They Would Do, Without Running Them
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30014v1.abstract: LLM agents with similar success rates can follow different action sequences. An Agent Behavior Map represents LLM-harness combinations using centered action log-likelihoods on shared reference trajectories, without requiring new environment rollouts from the target agent. We derive error bounds relating squared coordinate distances to trajectory KL under explicit assumptions, and across eight cross-scored models the distances track the directly measured trajectory KL in rank order. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30072v1.title: Charts as Epistemic Actions for Experience-Driven Agentic Data Analysis
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30072v1.abstract: Data agents built on ReAct-style loops now execute complex analytical workflows over structured data, yet their intermediate reasoning still runs almost entirely through text. Human analysts instead move between numbers, tables, and charts, reading visual evidence to expose trends and anomalies that text summaries drop. We ask whether charts can serve as internal epistemic actions inside a data agent's reasoning loop, and how to teach an agent to use them. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29822v1.title: UserSWE: Evaluating Coding Agents in Multi-Turn Conversations with Dynamic Users
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29822v1.abstract: As coding agents become more capable, developers increasingly use them to fix bugs through multi-turn interactions. Existing benchmarks do not adequately cover this scenario. Most present a complete issue report in a single turn without interaction. Their evaluation can produce both false positives and false negatives, accepting incorrect patches or rejecting correct ones. We introduce UserSWE for evaluating coding agents' ability to fix repository-level bugs through multi-turn interactions with dynamic users and execution-grounded verdicts at every turn. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29932v1.title: FrontierCS 2: A Benchmark for Computer Science R&D
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29932v1.abstract: Can LLM agents make contributions to frontier computer science R&D? We introduce FrontierCS 2, a benchmark of 48 open-ended tasks. We take a paper and the code its authors released and delete the paper's contribution. The deleted code becomes the human reference that sets the bar. Earlier open-ended benchmarks give each agent a problem statement and grade one program after the run. FrontierCS 2 places the agent inside a research environment. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29749v1.title: Metamodel-Guided LLM Decoding for Consistent DSL Generation
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29749v1.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate software engineering artifacts written in domain-specific languages (DSLs). Correct DSL instances usually must comply with not only the concrete syntax but also the abstract syntax defined by a metamodel augmented with semantic well-formedness constraints. Existing constrained decoding approaches typically guarantee compliance only with concrete syntax or with a limited set of semantic constraints expressed over the generated text, making metamodel-level constraint consistency difficult to enforce during generation. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30042v1.title: HGM-Dual: Lineage-Aware Guided Agent Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Planning
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30042v1.abstract: Harness optimization, which improves an agent's prompts, tools, and workflows, is an increasingly effective way to enhance agents built on frozen or closed-source LLMs. Leading approaches such as the Darwin--Godel Machine and the Huxley--Godel Machine (HGM) rely on recursive self-improvement and were developed mainly for coding, where the competence needed to improve the agent coincides with the competence being improved. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29823v1.title: MemoryTax: The Bitter Lesson of Agent Memory
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29823v1.abstract: Agent memory systems such as Mem0 and Zep decide what to keep before any question arrives; coding agents keep the raw history and let the model search it with its own tools. We ask whether designed memory still helps once the model is strong enough to search for itself. On one LoCoMo conversation (419 turns, 152 questions), we run four memory methods (full context, BM25, Mem0, Zep) and three coding agents (Pi, Codex, Claude Code), each with GPT-4o-mini, GPT-6 Luna and Claude Opus 5.5, and record what every rollout costs. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30103v1.title: Did the Problem Actually Get Harder? Testing LLMs on Paired P and NP-Complete Problems Hardened by Adversarial Multi-Agent Rewriting
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30103v1.abstract: Many NP-complete (NPC) problems have a polynomial-time (P) twin that differs in a single structural detail, such as 3- versus 2-colouring a graph. A model that reasons rather than recalls should notice which side of this boundary a problem falls on, yet existing benchmarks either fix the wording of each task or ignore its complexity class, so they cannot separate the two. We introduce P2NPCBench, a benchmark of 12 problem families in which every NPC problem is paired with a P twin posed over the same surface. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31080v1.title: nnInteractive Agent: General-Purpose AI Agents as 3D Image Annotators
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31080v1.abstract: Interactive 3D segmentation models such as nnInteractive turn a few spatial prompts (points, scribbles, boxes) into accurate volumetric masks, but a human still does the annotation work: finding each structure, placing prompts, checking the result and correcting it. General-purpose AI agents can now interpret images, call tools and write code. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30284v1.title: SWE-VERIFIER: Selective Verification for Cost-Efficient Coding Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30284v1.abstract: Coding agents spend substantial computation generating actions and processing long interaction histories. Poor action choices can steer agents into low-value states, wasting computation and increasing API costs. Sampling and verifying alternative actions can improve the agent's decisions, but applying this procedure at every step adds substantial overhead. We introduce SWE-Verifier, a lightweight generative model that selectively triggers candidate sampling and verification. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30557v1.title: Governed Self-Evolution for Autonomous Investing: A Multi-Agent LLM System with an Invariant Core
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30557v1.abstract: LLM agents that act on live Web data must combine heterogeneous evidence, remember what they have done and improve from outcomes without weakening their own safeguards. We study this problem in autonomous investing, where every action is irreversible and based on untrusted Web content. We present Steward, a multi-agent LLM system that draws the boundary of self-evolution in its type system. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30917v1.title: Harnessing Language Models as Optimization Modeling Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30917v1.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can translate natural-language optimization problems into solver programs, but reliably producing correct formulations and implementations remains challenging. Existing approaches improve optimization modeling through agentic workflows or task-specific post-training. This raises a practical question: can a lightweight harness using a single model role achieve competitive performance without additional training? http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31158v1.title: Beyond Watching and Searching: Benchmarking Agents for Video-centered Deep Research Reports
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31158v1.abstract: Deep research agents synthesize open-web evidence into long reports, but current benchmarks do not evaluate research centered on a source video. We introduce Video-Centered Deep Research Report Generation. Given a video and user request, an agent identifies research questions, retrieves external multimodal evidence, and produces an interactive report linked to relevant video moments. This task has direct practical value because it helps users locate relevant moments, verify claims, reproduce demonstrated procedures, and make informed decisions from video content. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30524v1.title: LLM2Cert: LLM Synthesis of Certificates with SMT/Lean Verification
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30524v1.abstract: Lyapunov functions and barrier certificates give state-space guarantees of stability and safety, but synthesizing and verifying them---especially for nonlinear, high-dimensional systems---remains an open challenge. Existing pipelines verify candidates with numerical solvers (sum-of-squares programs), interval methods, or satisfiability-modulo-theories (SMT) solvers, which often require relaxations, are conservative, or scale poorly with model dimension and nonlinearity. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30573v1.title: Diagnosing Personalization Failures in Mobile GUI Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30573v1.abstract: Unlike conventional GUI agents, personalized GUI agents require user preferences to guide sequential execution over changing GUI states. This raises two challenges: determining HOW each preference should alter execution strategy and WHEN it should take effect along the interaction trajectory. Existing benchmarks primarily evaluate overall task success, offering limited insight into these questions. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30355v1.title: CiteAnchor: Source-Aware Grounding for Hallucinated Citation Detection and Resolution
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30355v1.abstract: Hallucinated citations make it harder to trace sources and verify the evidence behind scientific claims. Detecting them is difficult because bibliographic records can be incomplete or differ across source types and publication versions. A plausible match alone neither validates the citation nor establishes its underlying source. We introduce CiteResolve, a benchmark of 423 real-world hallucinated citations annotated for source recoverability. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31120v1.title: SetCommit: Coordinated Token Commitments for Few-Step Diffusion Language Model Decoding
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31120v1.abstract: Diffusion language models generate multiple token positions in parallel, but few-step decoding makes parallel commitment difficult: tokens that appear reliable individually may be jointly inconsistent, while premature commitments can prevent later context-dependent refinement. In this paper, we introduce SetCommit, a training-free method for coordinated parallel token commitment. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30946v1.title: Tracing Hallucinations in LLM Reasoning for UML Class Diagram Generation: An Empirical Taxonomy and Mitigation Study
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30946v1.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate UML class diagrams from natural language requirements, but hallucinations may compromise the correctness and completeness of the resulting diagrams. Existing evaluations mostly assess the final diagram, without examining the intermediate traces of reasoning-capable LLMs, which can reveal where these hallucinations arise. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30412v1.title: SIM-UT: A User Simulation based Evaluation Framework for Medical Triage Chatbots
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30412v1.abstract: LLM-based chat agents are increasingly used for complex, multi-turn, multilingual medical triage in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet evaluation methods focus on single-turn, English-only benchmarks that primarily test the chatbots' knowledge. In practice, users are often confused, overwhelmed, or emotionally vulnerable, giving unclear, misspelled single-word answers or long messages in regional dialects, and the context of a conversation can shift rapidly. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30843v1.title: Lean Finder V2: Semantic Search for Mathlib That Disambiguates User Queries
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30843v1.abstract: We introduce Lean Finder V2, a semantic search framework for Mathlib that disambiguates user queries through complementary model-level adversarial training and input-level query rewriting. Human mathematicians and coding agents rarely search Mathlib by providing detailed context. In practice, they query short properties, notation, aliases, or hypotheses, leaving much of the intended mathematics implicit. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30491v1.title: What the Trace Shows and What the Label Says: Auditing Behavioral Detectors in Agent Evaluation
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30491v1.abstract: LLM agents are often evaluated by reducing execution traces to labels such as final-answer correctness, tool verification, and fault propagation. These labels are measurements produced by parsers, behavioral detectors, and harness rules, and they may not fully capture what the trace shows. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31511v1.title: DuoCook: An Overcooked-Inspired Benchmark for Visual Planning and Coordination
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31511v1.abstract: Coordinating two players in a cooking task requires a vision-language agent to track changing scene states, sequence recipe steps, and allocate shared resources under a time budget. We introduce an Overcooked-inspired benchmark for evaluating these capabilities in Unreal Engine environments constructed using coding agents. A single vision-language model controls both players from top-down visual observations, selecting high-level actions while the engine executes navigation. http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31148v1.title: Prompt Sensitivity in Tool-Augmented Model Comparisons
http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31148v1.abstract: Language models are compared on question-answering benchmarks that pose each question in one wording, and a reworded question can change which of two models scores higher.
